a: MIT is a short permissive license requiring copyright notice.
Apache-2.0 is permissive with an explicit patent grant.
GPL requires derivative works to stay under GPL when distributed.
Mixing licenses can block distribution — check before vendoring.
Ship required notices for bundled open source.
Proprietary keeps source closed; OSS publishes source under a license.
Some projects use a CLA so they can relicense contributions.
Code licenses do not automatically grant trademark rights.
Some projects offer OSS plus a commercial license.
